QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_27

question.text: Which statement correctly describes the base on which management fees are typically charged in an Indian Cat III AIF?

answer.text: Committed capital, regardless of whether called
Gross Net Asset Value (GNAV) at the end of the period, typically 1% to 2.5%
Only the profit above the hurdle rate
Residual value of unrealised investments (RVPI) only

explanation.text: The Logic: Category III AIFs charge management fees as a percentage of Gross Net Asset Value (GNAV) at the end of the period, typically in the range of 1% to 2.5% (illustrated by the worked annual fee example in the workbook). The Trap: Option A describes a committed-capital fee base. Option C confuses the management fee with the incentive fee. Option D mixes up fee base with a PE-style multiple. Note: The 1%-2.5% range and the GNAV fee base are taken from the management-fee illustration in the Cat III AIF workbook.
